name: Cascocauda
sum: Fluffy anurognathid from the Middle–Late Jurassic Tiaojishan Formation of Hebei, China, preserved with wing membranes and a dense coat of pycnofibres.
holotype: NJU-57003 — Mutoudeng locality (Daohugou bed), Tiaojishan Formation, Qinglong, Hebei.
material: Nearly complete articulated skeleton on main and counter slab.
exceptional: Extensive soft tissue: wing membranes and pycnofibres, some apparently branched like simple feathers (Yang et al. 2018).
biology: Short, wide ‘frog-like’ jaws with long thin teeth and large eyes — an aerial insect-hunter. Its tail is relatively long for an anurognathid.
author: Yang et al. 2022
dates_note: Age bracket from the stage named in the literature (ICS International Chronostratigraphic Chart); not in PBDB at time of download.
